keyFindings.description: keepStaleApproval drops a kept approval pair when the gate is nil. The first re-admission's ClearTreeGeneration deletes the gate, so a root re-admitted, parked again before its start was delivered, and re-admitted again loses the pair under an armed gate. Drop the pair only when a gate exists and holds no stale approval, or under gates.design off. Test it under an armed gate.

A catch-up computed before a queued root-architect start row forgets what it names will name the same decisions: the start is refused ErrDeliveryPending while a held task is pending, a ready arrives between RequestDeliver and forgetKept's commit, or the daemon crashes there. claimReady should leave out the marks a still-queued start row of the root names. Nothing is lost: if that row finishes without acting, the rows stay.

This is the tester's edge, and it is in scope. If forgetKept or the running-architect ClaimReady fails after the delivery, and the delivery is sent and retired before the retry, the retry queues the whole start task again, so the architect is told each decision twice. Mark the delivery processed in forgetKept's transaction, and skip RequestDeliver and the forget on a retry that finds the mark.

The outcome logging misreports. RelayNone (a no-person decision on a root that waits for its slot) and an unrecorded root log nothing, and a key handled before logs 'already sent to the controller' even when nothing was sent, because MarkProcessed now runs before the person check. The workflow switch also has no RelayNotParked line. parked-decision-verdict.jq reads these lines for the devbox proof, so an unmatched row fails the proof and a false 'sent' counts as a relay. Log every outcome on both paths, make the replay line say the key was handled before, and update the jq and its test.

TestOnlyADeliveredStartForgetsTheDecisionsItNamed stays green with the start path's forgetKept removed: bob's upsert replaces alice's row before the start runs. Name a second decision on another ref and assert that its row is gone after the delivery.

notFindings: Code-quality's branch shape of RelayParkedDecision, the slot lookup that now exists in three places, and the derived columns of a test table are maintainability items, not faults. The architect's Narrow decision leaves them out.

A listener of an earlier release answers 200 before it forwards, so during a rollout a catch-up forgotten on that 200 whose forward then fails, and whose copy a newer catch-up supersedes, can drop a decision. This exists only while an earlier-release listener is deployed. The daemon cannot tell that 200 from a delivery. It is the listener protocol's limit, not this change's.
